issues.legal_issue: Earth used for making bricks is a mineral that may be declared a minor mineral.
material_facts: The governing definition of minor mineral included ordinary clay and ordinary sand, as well as other minerals declared by the Central Government.
The Central Government declared brick-earth to be a minor mineral.
Brick-earth is earth used for making bricks.
issues.conclusion: Brick-earth is a mineral within the meaning of Section 3(e) of the Mines and Minerals (Regulation and Development) Act, 1957, and was correctly declared a minor mineral.
issues.legal_principle: A substance must first be a mineral before it can be declared a minor mineral under Section 3(e). “Mineral” has no fixed meaning and must be interpreted contextually; in this statutory context, its scope includes brick-earth, particularly because the definition includes ordinary clay and ordinary sand. The Court applied Bhagwan Das v. State of Uttar Pradesh, quoted Northern Pacific Railway Company v. John A. Soderberg, and quoted with approval Todd Birleston & Co. v. The North Eastern Railway Co. It approved Laddu Mal v. State of Bihar, Amar Singh Modilal v. State of Haryana, and Sharma & Co. v. State of Uttar Pradesh, and overruled State of West Bengal v. Jagdamba Prasad.

predicates.earth_used_for_making_bricks: The material is earth used to make bricks.
predicates.ordinary_clay_and_sand_are_minor_mineral: The governing definition treats ordinary clay and ordinary sand as minor minerals.
predicates.central_government_declared_the_earth_a_: The Central Government declared the brick-making earth to be a minor mineral.

issues.definition: When earth is used for making bricks, ordinary clay and sand fall within the minor-mineral category, and the Central Government declares that earth a minor mineral, the earth validly qualifies as a minor mineral.
